aboutGame.title: What is Gridlords?
paragraphs: Gridlords is a grid-based tactics game built around positioning, unit matchups, and turn-by-turn decision making. Instead of reflexes, it rewards planning: you deploy a squad, move pieces across a tactical board, manage resources between fights, and try to out-think your opponent rather than out-click them.

Battles mix single-player encounters with an async PvP autobattler mode, where you face saved squads and defense logic at your own pace. Early access keeps the roster, balance, and systems evolving, so our wiki tracks the current meta with guides, tier lists, and step-by-step walkthroughs.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about Gridlords.

items.question: What is Gridlords?
items.answer: Gridlords is a grid-based tactics game about positioning, unit matchups, and turn-by-turn decisions. You deploy a squad on a tactical board, manage resources between fights, and out-plan your opponent in single-player battles and async PvP autobattler matches.

items.question: How do I start playing Gridlords?
items.answer: Begin with the Gridlords Beginner Guide: learn the core run loop, keep fragile units behind cover, and plan the whole turn before you move. Winning the position first makes the damage easy.

items.question: Does Gridlords have PvP?
items.answer: Yes. Gridlords includes an async PvP autobattler mode where you fight a saved squad plus its defense logic, so you can play competitive matches at your own pace instead of in real time.

items.question: What is the best Gridlords build?
items.answer: There is no single best Gridlords build, but the strongest squads cover three jobs: a durable frontline anchor, reliable ranged damage, and control or support. Prioritize upgrades that reinforce your existing plan instead of spreading resources thin.

items.question: Where can I find Gridlords tier lists and patch coverage?
items.answer: The Gridlords Wiki collects unit tier lists, castle builds, item guides, and early access patch coverage, so you can check what changed before committing to a strategy.
